incidents.cause: A loss of tail rotor effectiveness while hovering in crosswind conditions resulting in the student pilot's loss of control of the helicopter, impact with terrain, and dynamic rollover.
The student pilot’s failure to maintain yaw control and the flight instructor’s delayed remedial action.
The pilot receiving instruction’s abrupt cyclic control input during the touch-down autorotation.
A loss of engine power for undetermined reasons, which resulted in a forced landing and impact with terrain.

The pilot’s failure to extend the landing gear before landing. Contributing to the accident were the pilot’s failure to use the Before Landing checklist due to being distracted while communicating with other aircraft and controlling the airplane in the gusting wind conditions.
